context:
Goal: only the batch runner marks a pull request ready, and the batch runner is never blocked by mistake.
Problem (rule): the new check stops a lane from marking its pull request ready; when it cannot read the session's own record, the lane built it to let the act through.
Based on (ruling): your fail-closed ruling of Oct 12 covers a guard whose script is missing, not a guard that cannot read a record, so no ruling covers this case.
Based on (read): refusing here would also block a batch runner whose record cannot be read.
Departs from: main has no ready check — adds one that lets the act through when the session record cannot be read.

options.gain: The batch runner is never stopped by a missing record.
options.how: When the session record cannot be read, the check allows marking ready.
options.label: Let it through (lane's pick)
options.lose: A lane with an unreadable record can mark its own pull request ready.

options.gain: No lane can mark a pull request ready by accident.
options.how: When the session record cannot be read, the check refuses and names the fix.
options.label: Refuse it
options.lose: A batch runner with an unreadable record stops until someone fixes the record.

reply: Closed 00:51 CST Nov 13 by triage: you accepted a (let it through). Sent to lane auto-merge-refused.
title: When the new ready check cannot read who a session is, does it let the session mark a PR ready?
why: The lane took this pick; it stands unless you choose b.
